## Guided Tutorial 15.2: The Cost-Center Budget Page

**Context and objective.** In this tutorial, you will build the page the department managers will read: each cost center's operating expense for fiscal 2026 against its budget. You will add the budget lines as a second fact table that shares Account, CostCenter, and Date with the ledger, mark the variances that need attention, and then explain them. A flexed budget will set aside the volume in the commission budget, a drill-through page will expose a cost that the budget and the ledger classify differently, and a reconciliation will show what remains. A visual calculation will show how the variance built up through the year.

**Prerequisites.** You need Charles River Reports.pbix from Tutorial 15.1, with the ledger star of Tutorial 14.3.

**Step-by-step instructions.**

**Step 1. Import the budget lines.**

a. Choose **Home > Get data > Excel workbook**, select CharlesRiver.xlsx, select **T77_BudgetLine**, and click **Transform Data**.
b. Rename the query `BudgetLine`, and keep BudgetLineID, FiscalYear, Month, AccountID, CostCenterID, BudgetAmount, BudgetCategory, and DriverType.
c. Open the filter on BudgetCategory, and clear **Balance Sheet**, so that only the income statement lines remain.
d. Choose **Add Column > Custom Column**, name the column `BudgetDate`, enter the formula below, and set its type to **Date**.
e. Choose **Home > Close & Apply**.

```
#date([FiscalYear], [Month], 1)
```

Each budget line now carries the first day of its month, the date through which the budget will relate to the calendar.

**Step 2. Relate the budget to the ledger's dimensions.**

a. In **Model view**, drag AccountID from **BudgetLine** onto AccountID in **Account**.
b. Drag CostCenterID from **BudgetLine** onto CostCenterID in **CostCenter**.
c. Drag BudgetDate from **BudgetLine** onto Date in the **Date** table.
d. Hide the two keys of BudgetLine.

@fig-15-07 shows the result. BudgetLine and GLEntry are two fact tables sharing three dimensions, so a visual grouped by cost center or account can place the budget beside the ledger.

![The Budget Beside the Ledger in Model View.](/visuals/svg/fig-15-07-budget-model.svg){#fig-15-07 fig-alt="A mock of Power BI's Model view. BudgetLine and GLEntry are two fact tables. Account, CostCenter, and Date each relate to both, many to one, with arrows pointing toward the fact tables. BudgetLine relates to Date on BudgetDate, the first day of each month, and GLEntry on PostingDate."}

**Step 3. Write the budget measures.**

a. Add the measures below to the Measures table, one at a time.
b. Format the first three as amounts and Variance % as a percentage with one decimal.

<!-- dax-check: measure -->
```
Budget = SUM ( BudgetLine[BudgetAmount] )
Actual = [GL Amount]
Variance = [Actual] - [Budget]
Variance % = DIVIDE ( [Variance], [Budget] )
```

Actual is the GL Amount of Tutorial 14.3, debits less credits without the closing entries, which for an expense account is the amount spent. Variance is actual less budget, so for an expense a positive variance is spending above the budget.

**Step 4. Compare each cost center with its budget.**

a. Add a page named `Budget`, with a slicer of Year set to 2026.
b. Add a matrix with CostCenterName on **Rows** and Budget, Actual, Variance, and Variance % as **Values**.
c. In **Filters on this visual**, add AccountSubType from Account and keep only Operating Expense.
d. Record the cost centers whose variance is more than five percent of their budget.

Three cost centers stand out. Sales spent far less than its budget, the Warehouse far more, and Administration less. Every other cost center is a few percent under budget. The (Blank) row holds the expenses budgeted and recorded without a cost center, such as rent, utilities, and insurance, which Chapter 7's Budget Table left out. Here both the budget and the actual amounts are present, and they agree within one percent.

**Step 5. Mark the variances that need attention.**

a. In the **Values** well, open the menu of Variance %, and choose **Conditional formatting > Icons**.
b. Set **Format style** to **Rules**, choose an icon set of arrows, and set **Icon layout** to the left of the data.
c. Write three rules, with **Number** values: at least 0.05, an arrow pointing up; greater than -0.05 and less than 0.05, a neutral circle; at most -0.05, an arrow pointing down.

@fig-15-08 shows the matrix. The markers differ in shape and sit beside the signed percentages, so they carry their meaning without color. The arrows point to the three cost centers a manager would ask about first.

![The Budget Matrix With Variance Markers.](/visuals/svg/fig-15-08-budget-matrix.svg){#fig-15-08 fig-alt="A mock of a Power BI matrix of fiscal 2026 operating expense by cost center, with columns for the budget, the actual amount, the variance, and the variance percentage. Each variance percentage has a marker beside it: an arrow pointing down for Sales and Administration, an arrow pointing up for the Warehouse, and a neutral circle for the other cost centers and the (Blank) row. The Sales, Warehouse, and Administration rows are outlined."}

**Step 6. Flex the commission budget.** The commission budget was calculated as a rate on the budget's sales volume, which Chapter 7 found to be several times the actual; flexing restates it at the actual volume.

a. Add the measure below, and format it as an amount.

<!-- dax-check: measure -->
```
Flexed Budget =
VAR CommissionBudget =
    CALCULATE ( [Budget], KEEPFILTERS ( Account[AccountNumber] = 6290 ) )
VAR CommissionRate =
    DIVIDE (
        CALCULATE ( [Budget], REMOVEFILTERS ( Account ), REMOVEFILTERS ( CostCenter ),
            Account[AccountNumber] = 6290 ),
        CALCULATE ( [Budget], REMOVEFILTERS ( Account ), REMOVEFILTERS ( CostCenter ),
            Account[AccountNumber] IN { 4010, 4020, 4030, 4040 } )
    )
VAR ProductRevenue =
    CALCULATE ( [Revenue], 'Item'[ItemGroup] <> "Services" )
RETURN
    [Budget] - CommissionBudget
        + IF ( NOT ISBLANK ( CommissionBudget ), CommissionRate * ProductRevenue )
```

Read the measure one variable at a time. CommissionBudget is the commission budget in the current filter context; KEEPFILTERS keeps it blank on any row that is not account 6290. CommissionRate divides the whole commission budget by the whole product revenue budget, with the filters on Account and CostCenter removed, which gives the rate the budget assumed. ProductRevenue is the actual revenue of the invoice lines without design services, which the commission budget did not include. The result replaces the commission budget with the rate times actual revenue and leaves every other budget line as it was.

**Step 7. Compare the spending with the flexed budget.**

a. Add the measure below, and format it as an amount.
b. Add Flexed Budget and Variance to Flexed to the matrix.

<!-- dax-check: measure -->
```
Variance to Flexed = [Actual] - [Flexed Budget]
```

The Sales cost center's flexed budget is less than half its static budget, and against the flexed budget its variance is small. The rate times actual product revenue reproduces the flexed commission of Chapter 7.

**Step 8. Drill through to the accounts.**

a. Add a page named `Cost Center Detail`, and drag CostCenterName into its drill-through well.
b. Add a matrix with AccountNumber and AccountName on **Rows** and Budget, Actual, and Variance as **Values**, filtered to Operating Expense.
c. On the Budget page, right-click the Warehouse row, and choose **Drillthrough > Cost Center Detail**.
d. Return, and drill through on Administration.

The Warehouse has a depreciation account with actual expense and no budget at all. Administration has a depreciation budget well above its actual depreciation. The two differences are equal and opposite: the company budgeted all of its depreciation in Administration and recorded part of it in the Warehouse, where the warehouse equipment is. The total is right; only the cost center differs.

**Step 9. Reconcile the variances.**

a. Add the measures below, formatting the first three as amounts and Remaining % as a percentage with one decimal.
b. On the Budget page, add a table visual with CostCenterName, Variance, Volume Effect, Classification Effect, Remaining Variance, and Remaining %.

<!-- dax-check: measure -->
```
Volume Effect = [Flexed Budget] - [Budget]
Classification Effect =
CALCULATE ( [Actual] - [Budget], KEEPFILTERS ( Account[AccountNumber] = 6130 ) )
Remaining Variance = [Variance] - [Volume Effect] - [Classification Effect]
Remaining % = DIVIDE ( [Remaining Variance], [Flexed Budget] )
```

@fig-15-09 shows the reconciliation. Each cost center's variance as booked is the sum of the volume in the commission budget, the classification of depreciation, and what remains. Volume Effect here is Chapter 7's sales-volume variance, not the volume effect of Chapter 6's margin bridge. The classification column adds up to zero across the cost centers, the signature of a classification difference: it moves cost from one cost center to another without changing the total. What remains is a few percent below budget nearly everywhere, the payroll burden rate that Chapter 7 found budgeted well above the actual rate. Sales remains further below budget than the others, because the actual commission rate on merchandise was also below the budgeted rate.

![The Variance Reconciliation by Cost Center.](/visuals/svg/fig-15-09-variance-reconciliation.svg){#fig-15-09 fig-alt="A mock of a Power BI table visual of fiscal 2026 operating expense by cost center, with columns for the variance as booked, the volume effect, the classification effect, the remaining variance, and the remaining variance as a percentage of the flexed budget. Sales has a large negative volume effect. The Warehouse and Administration have equal and opposite classification effects, and the classification column totals zero. The remaining percentages are small and negative for nearly every cost center."}

**Step 10. Show how the variance built up during the year.**

a. Add a table visual with YearMonth from Date and Variance to Flexed, filtered to 2026 and to Operating Expense.
b. With the table selected, choose **Home > New visual calculation**.
c. Type the formula below in the formula bar, and click **Back to report**.

<!-- dax-check: skip -->
```
YTD Variance = RUNNINGSUM ( [Variance to Flexed] )
```

The year-to-date column climbs in January, falls through June, climbs again in July, and falls for the rest of the year to the total of Step 9. January and July are the months with three pay dates, which Chapter 11 traced to payroll recorded when it is paid: against a budget that spreads salaries evenly, they look unfavorable, and every other month looks favorable. A manager who read the report in July would have seen a cost center on budget for the year; the months between tell the truer story. @fig-15-06 showed this calculation in the editor.

**Step 11. Add the budget test.**

a. In DAX query view, open the **Tests** tab, and add the query below at the end.
b. Run it, and save the report.

<!-- dax-check: query -->
```
// Test 4: the 2026 operating expense budget and actual must equal Chapter 7's
EVALUATE
CALCULATETABLE (
    ROW (
        "Budget", ROUND ( [Budget], 2 ),
        "Flexed Budget", ROUND ( [Flexed Budget], 2 ),
        "Actual", ROUND ( [Actual], 2 )
    ),
    'Date'[Year] = 2026,
    Account[AccountSubType] = "Operating Expense"
)
```

The budget equals the operating-expense budget lines of Chapter 7, including the lines without a cost center that its Budget Table left out, and the actual amount equals the operating expense of Tutorial 14.3. The flexed budget differs from the budget by exactly the change in the commission budget.

**Checkpoint.** Before you move on, confirm the following:

- BudgetLine relates to Account, CostCenter, and Date, and the Budget page compares each cost center's operating expense with its budget.
- The flexed budget restates only the commission budget, and Test 4 returns the budget, flexed budget, and actual amounts of Chapter 7 and Tutorial 14.3.
- The classification effect totals zero, and the remaining variance is a few percent below budget for nearly every cost center.

The department managers' page now answers their question and explains its own largest numbers. Without the flex and the reconciliation, the page would have rewarded Sales for a budget inflated by volume and blamed the Warehouse for a cost it was never budgeted.
